issues.legal_issue: A transferee cannot obtain substitution or addition under the rule governing transfers during the pendency of a proceeding when the transfer preceded the appeal and no application was made in the court where the suit was pending.
material_facts: The purchaser acquired the properties before the transferor filed the appeal.
The purchaser applied to be substituted or added in the appellate court, not in the court where the original suit was pending.
Even on the assumption that the suit remained pending until the decree was drawn up, no application to be brought on record was made in that suit.
issues.conclusion: The application could not be sustained under Order 22, rule 10: the transfer preceded the appeal, and no application had been made in the court where the suit was said to remain pending.
issues.legal_principle: Order 22, rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure applies to a transfer during the pendency of the suit or proceeding and requires an application in the court where the suit is pending. The Court considered the appellant's reliance on Lakshan Chunder Dey v. Sm. Nikunjamani Dassi but held that, even assuming the suit remained pending until the decree was drawn up, the application had not been made in that court; the later appellate application also fell outside the rule because the transfer preceded the appeal.

predicates.application_to_join_pending_appeal: A claimant applied to be substituted or added in an appeal that was already pending.
predicates.transfer_preceded_appeal: The transfer to the claimant occurred before the transferor filed the appeal.

issues.definition: When a claimant applies to join a pending appeal after receiving the relevant interest before the appeal was filed, the application is not maintainable under the rule for transfers during a proceeding.

issues.legal_issue: A person claiming through a transferor may continue an appeal filed by the transferor when the transferred interest carries the right to pursue that appeal.
material_facts: The owner transferred the properties to the claimant.
The transferor had filed an appeal concerning execution of a decree affecting those properties.
The claimant sought to be added to the pending appeal, although the claimant had not filed a separate appeal.
issues.conclusion: The claimant was entitled under section 146 of the Code of Civil Procedure to be brought on record and to continue the appeal filed by the transferor.
issues.legal_principle: Section 146 of the Code of Civil Procedure allows a proceeding that may be taken by a person to be taken by a person claiming under that person. An appeal is a proceeding for this purpose, and “claiming under” includes devolution and assignment of an interest. The provision is to be construed liberally to facilitate the exercise of rights acquired by devolution or assignment. The Court relied on Sitharamaswami v. Lakshmi Narasimha, approved in Jugalkishore Saraf v. Raw Cotton Co., Ltd., and on Muthiah Chettiar v. Govinddoss Krishnadoss; it also referred to Moidin Kutty v. Doraiswami.

predicates.pending_appeal: An appeal filed by one person remains pending before the court.
predicates.transferor_filed_appeal: The person from whom the claimant derives an interest filed the pending appeal.
predicates.claimant_succeeded_to_transferor_interes: The claimant acquired by transfer or devolution an interest held by the person who filed the appeal.

issues.definition: If an appeal filed by a person remains pending and a claimant succeeds to that person's relevant interest, the claimant may continue the appeal.

issues.legal_issue: A transferee whose property is directly affected by execution proceedings should be added to a pending appeal when substantial issues affecting that property remain to be determined and the transferee is bound by the proceedings.
material_facts: The claimant had purchased the properties for value under a deed reciting that they were free of encumbrances.
The decree holder later commenced proceedings to sell the properties under a mortgage decree.
The claimant disputed whether execution was barred by limitation and whether the amount claimed under the decree was recoverable from the properties.
The transferor had ceased contesting the decree holder's position, while the claimant was directly and substantially interested in the outcome and would be bound by the execution proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The claimant should be brought on record as an additional appellant to protect her interests in the pending appeal.
issues.legal_principle: A purchaser whose property is subject to execution proceedings may be bound by those proceedings, and justice requires that the purchaser have an opportunity to protect an interest directly affected by substantial issues still to be decided. The Court noted the court's power to transpose a party under Order 1, rule 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure or its inherent jurisdiction, referring to In re Mathews, Oates v. Mooney and Vanjiappa Goundan v. Annamalai Chettiar.

rule.if: pending_execution_appeal and transferee_owns_affected_property and substantial_issues_affect_property and transferee_bound_by_execution

predicates.pending_execution_appeal: An appeal is pending concerning execution of a decree against property.
predicates.transferee_owns_affected_property: A person acquired the property affected by the execution proceedings.
predicates.substantial_issues_affect_property: The appeal raises substantial unresolved issues about enforcement of the decree or the amount recoverable from the property.
predicates.transferee_bound_by_execution: The transferee's property interest may be affected by the execution proceedings regardless of whether the transferee participates.

issues.definition: When a transferee owns property affected by execution, may be bound by the proceedings, and substantial issues about that property remain in a pending execution appeal, the transferee is added to protect that interest.
